text:
incident-bot: PAGER: CRITICAL - cluster=infer-prod-eu pool=gpux-large
  metric=pre-fill_gpu_oom_count spike: 120 events in 5m, container restarts observed. Impact: ~12% error rate on long-context routes. Paging @alice_oncall and eng-runtime.

alice_oncall: ACK, joining incident. Jumping in to triage.

alice_oncall: Quick snapshot: repeated container restarts with CUDA errors during prefill stage. Logs show `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` and `SIGABRT` from prefill worker.

mike_runtime: Copying logs. Early hypothesis: KV prefetch + very long context (~>100k tokens) causing memory fragmentation + OOM during prefill.

sara_runtime: Can we temporarily stop KV prefetch for long-window routes and enable a conservative prefill trim? I can push a runtime flag.

alice_oncall: Good plan. @sara_runtime — do it. Also reduce concurrency on /v1/generate-prefill route to 1 per container as a live mitigation.

ramona_sre: Recommend not draining nodes immediately. Instead: 1) throttle noisy routes, 2) enable emergency fallback to coldmodel for >32k token requests, 3) scale out +2 GPU nodes. Draining would cause capacity churn.

logan_devex: I have a small hotfix that trims prefill window to 8k tokens and disables KV prefetch when client-supplied context > 8k. PR #4891 
  patch: `runtime.feature_flags.prefill_trim=8192` + `runtime.prefetch.enabled_for_large_context=false`

alice_oncall: Apply hotfix as canary (10% traffic) first. If canary reduces OOMs, roll to 100%. @ops-bot start canary deploy.

ops-bot: Deploy started: hotfix-prefill-trim v1.0 -> canary (10%)

(5m pass)

alice_oncall: Canary telemetry: OOM events on canary nodes down 85%, latency unchanged for small requests, large-context error rate down to ~3% in canary.

mike_runtime: Good signal. I'll wire up an automated router fallback to cpu-backed coldmodel for requests with context > 32k as an extra protection.

ops-bot: Canary successful. Rolling hotfix-prefill-trim v1.0 -> all (100%)

(15m pass)

ramona_sre: Cluster scaled: +2 gpux-large nodes added, autoscaler adjusted to prefer on-demand for next 30m. No further noisy restarts detected.

james_custsuccess: Notified top impacted customers (IDs: C-112, C-209, C-314) that we observed degraded generation on long-context routes and applied mitigations; ETA for stabilization ~30m. Customers acknowledged.

alice_oncall: Preparing handoff to evening oncall in 30m. Documenting actions and mitigation steps in the incident board.

nate_oncall: Thanks @alice_oncall — I will take over in 30 minutes and monitor for 2 hours. Please add any lingering TODOs.

alice_oncall: TODOs added to incident board:
  - postmortem with timeline (eng-runtime + eng-infra)
  - add automatic coldmodel fallback for >32k tokens (router)
  - add request size limit warning in SDKs and early reject option
  - kernel-level guardrail to avoid illegal mem accesses during prefill
  - improve prefetch heuristics to account for sequence length distribution

mike_runtime: Notes for postmortem: root cause likely interplay of KV prefetch + long-token sequences causing memory fragmentation and triggering CUDA illegal memory access during prefill. Action item: add memory accounting for prefill KV allocations + bounded prefetch window.

james_custsuccess: Customer update: no SLA breach expected at this point; monitoring continues.

alice_oncall: Handing over to @nate_oncall now. If anyone sees OOMs ramp again, ping @eng-runtime and @eng-infra and re-open pager.

incident-bot: INCIDENT status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident ID: INC-2024-2827.

nate_oncall: Oncall ack. Will keep watch.

(End of thread)
